thread:
incident-bot: :bangbang: INCIDENT 1751112222 detected - autoscaler oscillation + runtime GPU OOMs. Affected region: us-west-2. Impact: intermittent 5xx and high tail latency for hosted and dedicated customers. Pager: @annie.

annie: ACK. joining. summary pls?

raj: alerts spiked at 1751111800. ASG stretched 8 -> 36 in ~4m then collapsed to 9. lots of pods restarting with container crash logs showing CUDA OOM and 'kv-cache allocation failed'.

chloe: stack traces show runtime v2.4.0 trying to prefill KV cache on startup which blows memory for long-seq requests. CrashLoopBackOff prevalent on gpu nodes.

omar: i see node flaps too - kubelet evicting pods due to memory pressure then nodes becoming NotReady. Could be repeated heavy jobs + autoscaler policy too aggressive.

infra-bot: Detected scale events: 1751111765 ASG scaleUp +28, 1751111789 ASG scaleDown -27. Rapid consecutive changes flagged.

annie: immediate actions: 1) route mitigation 2) prevent further autoscale churn 3) reduce memory usage of restarting pods. Assign tasks.

ops-bot: applying edge rule: throttle concurrent requests for route group heavy-models to 8.

chloe: pushed a hotfix: set `--kv-prefill=false` on service heavy-model-prod-4 via emergency patch. Rolling to 2 pods first.

deploy-bot: emergency patch deployed to heavy-model-prod-4 (rollout id 1751112050). Canary pods healthy.

omar: recommend pausing cluster-autoscaler to stop feedback loop. we'll do manual scale to a safe window while we stabilize.

annie: pause autoscaler now. @deploy-bot /autoscaler pause -executor annie.

deploy-bot: /autoscaler pause confirmed at 1751112133 by annie.

raj: manual desired set to 14 nodes to absorb current steady load. @deploy-bot `cluster scale gpu-pool 14`.

deploy-bot: scale accepted. launching 5 nodes - ETA 5m.

chloe: also added a runtime fallback: route heavy-models -> cpu-quantized variant for non-enterprise tenants. That cut GPU pressure a lot.

annie: note to CS - notify customers impacted by 5xx. @cs-alex please escalate to top affected tenants.

cs-alex: notifying now. drafting message: "We're investigating increased errors in us-west-2; we've applied mitigations and will follow up."

omar: cordoned 4 noisy nodes (gpu-7, gpu-12, gpu-18, gpu-23) and drained them. Observed fewer restarts after cordon. Some pods still OOM during init due to prefill; hotfix rollout helped.

raj: observed kernel logs: `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79` repeated alongside 'out of memory' markers. Collecting dmesg and pod logs to /var/tmp/incs/1751112222_logs.tar.gz.

chloe: pressure dropped GPU mem 95% -> 68% over 8m after throttles + fallback + prefill off. Error rate down ~75%. latency still jittery for hosted-premium.

annie: temporary policy: keep autoscaler paused for 30m, maintain node count 14. Bind a dampening PR to autoscaler policy to limit deltas >10 nodes per 10m.

infra-bot: creating ticket INFRA-1751: autoscaler damping default to 10 nodes / 10m.

omar: long term: we need a batching gate for big-seq jobs and client-side chunking recommended. Also protect runtimes from prefill on restart unless memory headroom present.

chloe: capturing rollback option: if hotfix causes regressions, we can revert to runtime v2.3.8 which doesn't prefill. but v2.3.8 lacks some perf wins. hold for now.

annie: postmortem owner: raj + chloe. add timeline + root cause hypotheses. I'll coordinate.

ops-bot: incident status -> mitigated, severity -> P2 at 1751112980. Monitoring for 60m.

annie: thanks team. keep channel active for any regression. I'll post an initial incident summary to #incidents-summary in 30m. :white_check_mark:

chloe: one small action item: add health-check backoff for services so they don't aggressively restart when kernel OOMs persist. filing ENG-rt-987.

raj: saved traces and docker logs in S3: s3://redwood-incidents/1751112222/ for the postmortem.

incident-bot: closing incident thread for active mitigation - monitoring window open until 1751116580.
